reasoning_traces.think:
Perceptual illusions arise from misalignment between sensory input and cognitive interpretation. The system's probabilistic nature allows for multiple valid interpretations, but only one is selected based on associative memory and attentional weighting. This leads to systematic errors in perception, particularly when sensory cues are ambiguous or conflicting. The failure mode occurs when top-down expectations override bottom-up sensory evidence, resulting in misclassification of visual features. The mathematical framework treats perception as a Bayesian inference problem where priors derived from past experience influence current sensory interpretation. Sensory data is modeled as a noisy signal corrupted by associative biases and attentional limitations. The breakdown regime manifests when the posterior distribution becomes multimodal or when the likelihood function fails to capture true sensory states. These primitives form a coherent basis for understanding how sensory systems interact with higher-order cognition to produce stable yet fallible perceptions.
